newsitem.title: UK: Scotia bounces after Lehman recommendation.
newsitem.headline: Scotia bounces after Lehman recommendation.

text.p: Shares in Scotia Holdings Plc rose on Thursday, rebounding from recent weakness as analysts at Lehman Brothers recommended the stock, dealers said.

The stock was up 18-1/2p at 452-1/2 by 1138 GMT in volume of 225,352 shares, after tumbling to a two-year low of 325p on March 11 after the biotechnology group said regulators were unwilling to approve Tarabetic, one of its key drugs.
Scotia chief executive David Horrobin said earlier this week he remained confident about the company's drug pipeline and believed Tarabetic would ultimately win approval in Britain.

Lehman analyst Stewart Atkins said the rejection of diabetes treatment Tarabetic by the Medicine Controls Agency "seems to have galvanised Scotia into putting in place a number of interesting measures."
He said the company had improved management controls by splitting into four business units and had focused on a smaller number of clininal areas, ending concerns that Scotia was spread too thinly.
The announcement of collaborative partners and progress in photodynamic therapy Foscan were other positives, along with its vigorous defense of the "lipid" technology behind Tarabetic, Atkins said.
The Lehman analyst gave the stock a "venture-outperform" rating and set a year-end target of 603p assuming minimal value for Tarabetic.
